originality.rationale: The same map appears in the full-text 2022 defining article and the lambda=1 specialization of a full-text 2025 generalization, but their inspected claims and calculations concern fixed points, early doubling and numerical diagrams; neither yields the unique positive sextic root giving a superattracting primitive three-cycle or a rigorously uniform attracting-three band. Existing historical work on this map addresses primitive two- and four-cycle behavior, not these period-three statements. General unimodal-map theory does not imply the explicit algebraic uniqueness or parameter interval. Priority beyond checked accessible sources remains unproven.
residual_risks: Some earlier or unindexed rational-map analyses could contain equivalent algebraic parameter values or stronger periodic-window certificates.

value.rationale: The new structural invariant is the unique superstable primitive-three parameter of an established rational logistic family and an analytically certified open stable-three subinterval, not arbitrary finite sampling or an unmotivated decimal. It corrects the impression that numerically reported high-amplitude chaotic onset could exclude attracting period-three windows, without denying coexistence with chaotic invariant sets; the exact algebraic root and rational contraction region provide reproducible benchmarks for bifurcation analysis.
